charts.title: A qubit stored in a repeating pattern
charts.label: Ideal-code schematic
charts.summary: Even sites represent logical 0; odd sites represent logical 1. A displacement of L changes logical parity.
charts.explanation: The vertical lines indicate ideal peak locations, not finite-height probability densities. The lower strip is the simulator's readout rule for a residual shift relative to the intended code state. An ideal final correction removes the within-cell offset; an odd remaining cell index is a logical error.

charts.title: What encode_gkp actually builds
charts.label: Actual encoder output
charts.summary: A 17 × 17 coherent-state sum, an energy envelope, and a normalized vector of 100 amplitudes.
charts.explanation: The left plot shows centers of the 289 coherent-state terms and the signs of their amplitudes. It is not the final state's probability distribution. The center plot shows the finite-energy filter. The right plot is the normalized Fock-level probability from the actual encode_gkp(0.30, 100, 8) output (display zoomed to n ≤ 60). This function prepares approximate logical zero, rather than an arbitrary input qubit or a physical preparation circuit.
charts.code:
coeffs += (-1)**(k * ell) * coherent_state
coeffs *= exp(-delta**2 * n)
coeffs /= norm(coeffs)

charts.title: Finite energy turns ideal spikes into peaks
charts.label: Actual encoder output
charts.summary: Changing Δ changes the shape and energy of the prepared quantum state.
charts.explanation: These position probability densities are calculated from the encoder's complex Fock coefficients using harmonic-oscillator wavefunctions. Smaller Δ gives narrower peaks and a broader overall envelope. All three states use 240 Fock levels and k_max = 12 for this comparison. The plotted position range is cropped; the densities have not been renormalized to that crop. Δ is a state-preparation parameter and is separate from the noise engine's σq and σm.
charts.code:
psi_q = sum(c_n * harmonic_oscillator_wavefunction(n, q))
P_q = abs(psi_q)**2

charts.title: See the quantum state in phase space
charts.label: Actual encoder output
charts.summary: The center is a Wigner function; the side curves are ordinary position and momentum probability densities.
charts.explanation: Red and blue represent positive and negative Wigner values. Negative regions describe quantum interference, not negative probabilities of measurement outcomes. The marginals are nonnegative. This is the actual encoder state computed by QuTiP; the main decoder benchmarks do not evolve this full Wigner function each round. Axis coordinates are divided by L, while the Wigner values retain QuTiP's q,p normalization.
charts.code:
psi = encode_gkp(0.30, 100, 8)
W = qutip.wigner(psi, q_grid, p_grid)

charts.title: The three signals inside the noise engine
charts.label: Seeded illustration
charts.summary: A physical kick, its fresh random component, and a separate measurement error.
charts.explanation: This is trial 0 (zero-based) from 32 trials using seed 20261117; the same path is used in the decoding walkthrough. The shaded bands are distribution standard deviations, not confidence intervals or hard bounds. The first displacement is sampled directly from the stationary distribution, so a separate innovation is not plotted for round 1. dₜ is a per-round kick, not the accumulated position x.
charts.code:
d[0] = Normal(0, sigma_q)
d[t] = rho*d[t-1] + Normal(0, sigma_q*sqrt(1-rho**2))
nu[t] = Normal(0, sigma_m)

charts.title: Memory changes the texture of noise
charts.label: Seeded illustration
charts.summary: Increasing ρ creates persistent runs while keeping the long-run displacement variance fixed.
charts.explanation: These three paths use common standard-normal random draws and the same σq. Higher ρ gives the next kick a stronger dependence on the previous kick. Each finite path can have a different sample mean or sample variance even though their stationary distributions have the same zero mean and SD. Correlation is not the same as a larger noise amplitude.

charts.title: How much noise, and how much memory?
charts.label: Analytic curves
charts.summary: The width of a distribution and its correlation over time are separate properties.
charts.explanation: The left curves are exact Gaussian densities for the default parameters. The right curves are the exact stationary AR(1) autocorrelations, not estimates from one short path. Independent measurement noise has correlation zero at every nonzero lag, the same shape as the ρ = 0 curve. Neither plot is an experimental device measurement.

charts.title: The engine can change its noise conditions
charts.label: Seeded illustrations
charts.summary: Regime switching, slow drift, and sudden bursts are separate stress-test mechanisms.
charts.explanation: These are illustrative samples from the repository's extension modules, not completed-study results. Switching changes correlation through a hidden two-state Markov chain. The ramp changes the target displacement variance while rescaling the AR state. A burst adds a separate kick during its active rounds; that kick is not fed into later AR noise. The displacement it causes can remain in the oscillator until corrected.
charts.code:
d_t = AR_displacement_t + burst_sd_t * fresh_normal
# the extra burst is not part of the next AR state

charts.title: A small shift: the nearest-lattice correction succeeds
charts.label: Constructed teaching example
charts.summary: Physical shift 0.15L + readout error 0.05L → syndrome +0.20L → residual -0.05L.
charts.explanation: These values were chosen to explain the arithmetic; they are not a sampled benchmark. Pale green cells have even nearest-lattice index, and pale red cells have odd index. Readout error changes the measured value. It affects the physical state indirectly when the decoder acts on that value. The logical-error rule assumes an ideal final within-cell correction.
charts.code:
x_pre = x_prev + d
s = wrap(x_pre + nu)
c = s
x_after = x_pre - c

charts.title: A larger shift: wrapping can hide a logical error
charts.label: Constructed teaching example
charts.summary: Physical shift 0.60L + readout error 0.05L → syndrome -0.35L → residual +0.95L.
charts.explanation: These values were chosen to explain the arithmetic; they are not a sampled benchmark. Pale green cells have even nearest-lattice index, and pale red cells have odd index. Readout error changes the measured value. It affects the physical state indirectly when the decoder acts on that value. The logical-error rule assumes an ideal final within-cell correction.
charts.code:
x_pre = x_prev + d
s = wrap(x_pre + nu)
c = s
x_after = x_pre - c

charts.title: Why decoding needs more than one measurement
charts.label: Exact mapping + teaching example
charts.summary: The syndrome reveals the offset within a cell. The decoder must infer the cell's parity.
charts.explanation: The left curve is the actual wrap function. All four marked inputs yield s = −0.35L. The right panel returns to the constructed +0.60L displacement with +0.05L readout error: corrections c = s and c = s + L lead to different logical outcomes. History changes which choice is plausible; it does not reveal the hidden noise directly.
charts.code:
s = (x + nu + L/2) % L - L/2
c = s + j*L  # j is 0 or 1

charts.title: Watch memory change a correction decision
charts.label: Selected seeded trajectory
charts.summary: At round 34, nearest lattice is in an odd cell while matched Bayes is in an even cell.
charts.explanation: This is trial 0 from a seeded set of 32 paths. It was selected because it contains a round where nearest lattice is logically wrong and Bayes is correct. It illustrates a mechanism and does not estimate decoder performance. The true residuals shown here are diagnostics; neither decoder sees them. A residual near −2L is in an even cell and is logically correct under the ideal-code scoring rule.
charts.code:
NL: c = s
Bayes: c = s + j*L
error = round(x_after/L) % 2

charts.title: What the Bayesian decoder believes
charts.label: Actual grid-filter posterior
charts.summary: The filter gives the j = 1 correction class ≥99.9% posterior probability at the selected round.
charts.explanation: This posterior comes from the repository's 128-point Bayesian grid filter after processing the syndrome history. We sum over hidden displacement and express position relative to the base correction c = s. The middle green region supports j = 0; the outer red regions support j = 1. The two plot edges meet because position is periodic modulo 2L. These are model beliefs, not measured error frequencies or guarantees. Grid discretization and assumed noise parameters affect the belief.
charts.code:
predict noise → shift position belief → multiply by syndrome likelihood
normalize posterior
j = 1 if posterior_mass_of_class_1 > 0.5 else 0

charts.title: The binary-readout extension
charts.label: Analytic measurement model
charts.summary: A one-bit measurement is sampled from a periodic probability curve.
charts.explanation: This is the PhaseBit model used by the closed-loop extension. The graph shows the probability of observing bit 1, not a logical-error probability. Visibility below one reduces measurement contrast. A readout bit flip further mixes the outcomes; in this simple curve, visibility 0.8 and independent flip probability 0.1 produce the same effective contrast, so those two curves coincide. Full ancilla dynamics and back-action are not simulated here.
charts.code:
p1 = (1 - visibility*cos(2*pi*(x + nu)/L)) / 2
bit = Bernoulli(p1)
bit ^= Bernoulli(p_flip)

charts.title: How the current code fits together
charts.label: Code architecture
charts.summary: State construction and decoder benchmarking are separate computational paths.
charts.explanation: The encoder constructs a one-oscillator quantum state. The main simulator tracks one classical residual displacement x in the q quadrature, initialized at zero, and evaluates a decoder against synthetic noise. The state-preparation parameter Δ does not automatically feed into σq or σm. The shift loop omits finite-energy state evolution, the p-quadrature error channel, photon loss, and detailed ancilla back-action. Separate finite-energy checks in the repository investigate some connections between the two representations.
charts.code:
quantum/encoding.py → quantum state and visual diagnostics
simulator/noise.py → simulator/sim.py → decoder → logical-error record
